clue.text: Senile litigant upset the chattering classes

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly person suing someone annoys the talkative elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the fourteen letters of SENILE LITIGANT; 'the chattering classes' is the definition, not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The chattering classes is a mocking name for educated people who discuss ideas and politics, the intellectual elite.

clue.text: Giving a recital managed to raise standing

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so it is read backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
a rating is one's standing or rank

explanation.surface: A performer wants a recital to improve their reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' turns RAN into NAR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrating means telling a story aloud, giving an account or recital of events.

clue.text: Provide bear with no resistance

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: to bear something is to endure it
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Feed a bear with no fight in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes R from ENDURE. 'bear' looks like the animal but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue someone with a quality is to endow or supply them with it.

clue.text: Interest uninitiated in leanings of representatives

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: a ship lists when it leans

indicators.note: uninitiated means without its initial, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a hobby is a pastime or interest

explanation.surface: Novices with an interest in political leanings of elected members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks like concern for the subject but is a pastime; 'leanings' looks like opinions but is a ship listing. 'uninitiated' drops the first letter and 'in' sets the shortened pastime within.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobbyists are paid agents who represent interest groups to lawmakers.

clue.text: Don't be such a baby when dismissing wife's family

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: grow up is what you say to someone acting childishly
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone tells a spouse's relatives to stop acting childishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes the W from GROW UP. 'wife's family' looks like in-laws; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of related things, as in a language group, is a family.

clue.text: Almost time left to be picked up by young fox in disco

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost

indicators.note: being picked up by means being held by, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a young fox is a cub

explanation.surface: Late at night, a youngster is picked up at a dance venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be picked up by' puts L inside CUB, making CLUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a nightclub where people dance to recorded music.

clue.text: Religious teacher bathed self

parts.note: to bathe is to go for a swim, so swam
I is one's self

explanation.surface: A holy man takes a dip by himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man.

clue.text: Gives idiot mixed gins

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foolish pours a cocktail of gins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges GINS to IGNS. 'Gives' is the definition, not part of the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign something is to allot or give it.

clue.text: Be uplifted by Crosby's decline

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting a word lifts it upward, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Bing Crosby was the American crooner

explanation.surface: A crooner's career is lifted from a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifted' turns BE into EB; BING is the first name of Bing Crosby.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbing means receding or dwindling, falling into decline like an outgoing tide.

clue.text: Tried for some time and made a deep impression

explanation.surface: Someone persevered at something and left a lasting mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wearied by something tedious over a long time is one sense; drilling a hole deep into a surface is the other.

clue.text: Sounds of impact entertaining rowdy coaches

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a host holds guests, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bams are the noises of a collision or blow
rowdy behaviour is rough

explanation.surface: Loud crashes come from a boisterous group of sports coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coaches' looks like sports trainers but means horse-drawn carriages; 'entertaining' has the crash sounds hold the rowdy word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a kind of coach.

clue.text: Occupying an English city without reason

parts.note: occupying a place is being in it
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Settling in a provincial cathedral city for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a silly, pointless way is acting without reason or sense.

clue.text: Rewrite start of sharply worded positioning

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is written afresh as a different letter

parts.note: a cutting remark is sharply worded and hurtful

explanation.surface: An editor asks for the opening of a harsh piece to be redone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rewrite start of' swaps the C at the front of CUTTING for P.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something somewhere is placing or positioning it.

clue.text: Golden-voiced in remorse

indicators.note: voiced means spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: gilt means covered in gold, golden

explanation.surface: A singer with a beautiful voice is full of regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden-voiced' reads as praise for a singer; split it, and 'voiced' tells you GILT is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling remorse is feeling guilty: the sense of having done wrong.

clue.text: Ms Hudson sat out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman named Hudson sat it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ms' looks like a title for a woman; it is the plural of M, the Roman numeral for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: M stands for a thousand, so several Ms are several thousands.

clue.text: Sings about spring growths

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a spring is a natural source of water, a well

explanation.surface: Someone sings about the season of new growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a water source, and 'about' wraps the singing word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swellings are lumps or bulges on the body, abnormal growths.

clue.text: Resented a shabby person living in the right part of town?

definitions.text: person living in the right part of town?

indicators.note: shabby means run-down and disordered, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A poor resident of a smart district resents being looked down on.
explanation.walkthrough: London's East End lies to the right on a map; 'right' looks like 'smart' but means the east side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Londoner from the East End, the eastern side of the city, which sits on the right of a map.

clue.text: Contradictions for one entering States

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the second piece goes into the first

parts.note: nations are states
e.g. means for example, for one

explanation.surface: Disagreements arise when one person enters a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' is the standard crossword way to give e.g.; 'entering' takes it into the word for States.
explanation.definitionFit: A negation is a denial, the contradicting of a statement.

clue.text: Takes in unlimited rent receipts

indicators.note: unlimited means with its boundaries removed, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: grosses are total takings or receipts

explanation.surface: A landlord collects unlimited rent payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' trims RENT to EN, which is then followed by GROSSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross is to absorb the attention entirely, to take someone in.

clue.text: Rely on poorly run test

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: You cannot depend on a badly conducted trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' rearranges RUN TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrust something to someone is to hand it over in reliance on them, placing trust in them.

clue.text: Secretly record the French horn

parts.note: to bug a room is to plant a hidden microphone to record
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Bugging a French horn player's private conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French horn' looks like the instrument; 'the French' gives LE and 'horn' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a simple brass horn used for military signals.

clue.text: Chirac's base among cheesy leaders from the right

indicators.note: from the right says the hidden letters are read backwards
among says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A French president's headquarters is full of corny politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'among' in the definition; it is the hiding signal. Inside 'cheesy leaders' sits EESYLE, read from the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysee Palace in Paris is the official residence of the French president, the post Jacques Chirac held.

clue.text: More faithful taking up empty seats in tier

indicators.note: taking up means absorbing, so the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: truer means more loyal or faithful

indicators.note: empty means hollowed out, leaving just the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A more loyal fan occupies vacant seats in the stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tier' looks like a row of seats in the surface but is read as one who ties. 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of 'seats'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusser binds things up with rope or string, so is someone who ties, a tier.

clue.text: Upper-class jerk comes to a Carthaginian city

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A posh fool arrives at an ancient North African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like a fool but means a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Utica was an ancient Phoenician city near Carthage that fell under Carthaginian rule.

clue.text: Put back some of Louvre's etchings

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A curator returns some prints to the Paris museum.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset something is to set it again, to put it back in place.

clue.text: Feeling myself back on road to recovery at last

indicators.note: back means turned around, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: me stands for myself
a path is a road or way

indicators.note: at last means take only the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone senses they are finally on the road to recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM; 'at last' takes Y from 'recovery'.
explanation.definitionFit: Empathy is the feeling of sharing and understanding another person's emotions.

clue.text: Mountain climbing in the veldt?

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing goes upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain, as in the Swiss Alps

explanation.surface: A mountaineer goes up a peak in South African grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ALP to PLA. The veldt is the open grassland of southern Africa, hence the question mark: it is one example of a plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The veldt is open grassland in southern Africa, a typical example of a broad flat plain.

clue.text: Organised workers discharged?

explanation.surface: Workers who joined a trade union find themselves dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as UN-IONISED, the word means having no ions, i.e. electrically discharged; the question mark flags that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers brought into a trade union are unionised; something not ionised carries no electrical charge, so is discharged.

clue.text: To-do to do with love

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or ado
re means concerning or to do with

explanation.surface: A fuss about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply.

clue.text: Ephemeral quality in Norse artists' works

indicators.note: works as a verb means kneads or shapes, so the letters before it are reshaped

explanation.surface: There is something fleeting about the works of Scandinavian painters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun for paintings but is the anagram signal for IN NORSE ARTISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ephemeral means lasting only a short time, the quality of being fleeting.
